# LLMReady

> An open-source spec-compliance auditor for AI discovery. It validates /llms.txt, RFC 9309 robots.txt policy, static HTML signal-to-noise and schema.org metadata, then returns the exact source line and a copy-paste fix for every miss.

LLMReady runs against the initial HTML response. It does not execute JavaScript against the target and does not store audits in a database. The public instance is free, open source and has no signup.

## What the audit measures

### Discovery & manifests

- `/llms.txt` is fetched as plain text and validated for one H1, a blockquote summary, H2 sections, a markdown link index and pagination markers.
- `/llms-full.txt` is treated as an optional single-request context bundle. It must be plain text, usable and unpaginated.
- `/sitemap.xml` is parsed, including sitemap indexes, and must contain URLs. The audit also checks for a `Sitemap:` directive in `robots.txt`.

### Crawler access

RFC 9309 matching is implemented directly: the longest matching path wins, `Allow` wins ties, and both `*` and `$` syntax are supported. The audit evaluates `GPTBot` (OpenAI), `ClaudeBot` (Anthropic), `Google-Extended` (Google), `PerplexityBot` (Perplexity) and `Bytespider` (ByteDance). It also checks for an explicit named AI policy, `robots` meta directives and a blocking `X-Robots-Tag` response header.

### Static parseability

- Exactly one H1 in the content region.
- Heading sequence without skipped levels.
- Static HTML signal-to-noise ratio of at least 65 percent of visible text. Content text is measured against navigation, header, footer, aside, banner, consent-widget and `aria-hidden` text.
- At least 600 characters of readable text in the initial HTML response.

Content is read from `main`, else `[role="main"]`, else the richest `article`, else `body`. A region that only holds a teaser falls back to the full document. Scripts, styles, SVGs, forms, frames and hidden nodes are removed before measurement.

### Structured data

- JSON-LD blocks are parsed and checked for `@context` and `@type`.
- The audit looks for one of `TechArticle`, `FAQPage` or `SoftwareApplication`.
- `/openapi.json`, `/.well-known/openapi.json` and `/openapi.yaml` are probed for OpenAPI documents.
- `/.well-known/security.txt` and `/.well-known/ai-plugin.json` are checked as optional discovery surfaces.

## Scoring

Each check returns pass, warn or fail, worth 100, 50 or 0 points. A pillar score is the weighted average of its checks. The overall score is the mean of the four pillars: discovery, access, parseability and structured data. Grades are A (90-100), B (75-89), C (60-74), D (40-59) and F (0-39).

## Workspace

The audit matrix shows every check with its protocol, source file, exact line number, a short observation and an expandable code fix. The `llms.txt` editor builds both the manifest and the full bundle from the pages discovered during the audit, validates the result and offers copy and download actions. The scraper simulator shows the raw HTML beside the cleaned markdown a non-JS crawler would ingest, with payload reduction and token estimates.

## API

`GET /api/audit?url=example.com` returns a JSON report with:

- `score`, `grade`, `gradeLabel` and four `pillars`.
- Each check with `id`, `label`, `status`, `summary`, `detail`, `protocol`, `weight`, `evidence` and an optional `fix`.
- `evidence.file`, `evidence.line` and `evidence.snippet` for line-level evidence.
- `fix.language` and `fix.code` for a copy-paste resolution.
- `profile`, `pages`, `files`, `vision`, `fixes` and `meta`.

A bare domain or a full URL is accepted. Errors use `{ "error": { "code", "message", "hint?" } }`. Identical URLs are cached for five minutes per server instance. The public rate limit is 30 audits per minute per IP.

## Standards and source

- llms.txt specification: https://llmstxt.org/
- RFC 9309: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9309
- schema.org: https://schema.org/
- Source code: https://github.com/aiden/llm-seo-toolbox
